methods.name: Signal restoration
methods.consequence: A known original sign and the received magnitude restore either original without diagnosis: cost 1 for a positive original, 2 for a negative original, against diagnosis at 3.

nodes.text: For original x ≠ 0, received y ∈ {x, −x}, and known original sign σ, the supplied restoration is σ|y| = x.

children.text: For x > 0, σ = +1 and |y| = x. For x < 0, σ = −1 and −|y| = x.

All four pairs of intervening reversals are repaired for either original sign. Positive magnitude costs 1. Composing it with the existing one-unit sign reversal costs 2 for a negative original; diagnosis costs 3.

nodes.text: The earlier negative-source counterexample defeats positive magnitude, not magnitude-based restoration. Constructing negative magnitude completes the missing half of the method.

children.text: When the original is −7, |−7| = +7 is wrong, but −|−7| = −7 and −|+7| = −7 both restore it.

If both +7 and −7 remain possible originals and their original sign is unavailable, the same received +7 can require either restoration. The missing sign cannot be recovered from that received value alone.

methods.name: Calculation repair
methods.consequence: All eight calculation repairs return 0.06. Missing-part observation plus its matching repair costs 2; layout-first costs 3 for the same result.
methods.expression: missing rule → supplied rule; missing input → supplied input; result = 0.06

nodes.text: Each record requires 10.06 − 10.00. The supplied plan observes whether its rule or input is missing and installs that component. Every executed record then returns 3/50.

children.text: The observation costs 1 and either repair costs 1. Four layouts change neither repair nor result, so the worst total cost is 2 across all eight records.
When the omission is already known, the matching repair costs 1. Repeating the missing-part observation adds work without changing the completed result.

nodes.text: The constructor compares complete repairs with every distinguishing inquiry followed by its complete answer branches. Its selected cost is the minimum worst-case total among the supplied alternatives.

children.text: An inquiry's total is its own cost plus its most costly completed answer branch. Every branch ends in an actual repair adequate for all remaining cases.
If an indistinguishable group has no common successful repair, the constructor returns that group as an obstruction. An empty branch is never counted as successful completion.

methods.name: Tooling construction
methods.consequence: Including the tool’s own prerequisite moves its production advantage from two items to four. The completed route includes bootstrap, production, and maintenance.

nodes.text: Manual production costs 4n. The complete tooling route costs 9 + n + 2⌊(n−1)/3⌋, including the four-unit bootstrap part that the tool cannot produce before it exists.

children.text: At n = 1, the costs are 4 and 10. At n = 2, they are 8 and 11. At n = 3, both cost 12. At n = 4, they are 16 and 15.
The complete tooling route remains cheaper for every integer n ≥ 4. The first-item comparison therefore selects a different method from the complete four-item undertaking.

nodes.text: A constructor can depend on another constructed capability. Completing the upstream dependency changes what the downstream method can actually produce.

children.text: A repeated expert correction is a consumed contribution when every usable result needs it. With B available units and e units consumed per result, unreplenished support permits at most ⌊B/e⌋ results.

The website's earlier producer required two levels of labels before its knowledge. Removing those compulsory fields changes every generated method page; editing one finished page would have left the producer able to recreate the defect.

methods.name: Continuous operation
methods.consequence: With withdrawals of 0–2, the low/high policy preserves levels 1–9 indefinitely. The exact-level policy reaches 4–6 within three periods and preserves it.

nodes.text: For x ≤ 4, u = 2 gives a next level between 1 and 6. For x ≥ 5, u = 0 gives a next level between 3 and 9. Both branches preserve 1–9 after every admitted withdrawal.

children.text: The two branches use the low/high observation only. Exact measurement is unnecessary for this guarantee.
For the narrower target, u(x) = min(3, 6−x). At levels 4, 5, and 6 it supplies +2, +1, and 0; at high levels the model admits removal. Every start in 1–9 reaches 4–6 within three periods.

nodes.text: Continued operation includes the conditions that keep its actions available. With two stations that each serve twice before repair, a fully occupied lone worker exhausts the initial four-service capacity.

children.text: A second worker supplies concurrent repair. Serving at one usable station while repairing the other preserves a usable station for the next period.
Every initial wear pair except both fully worn supports the continuous policy. The labor and starting-state conditions remain part of this construction.

methods.name: Coverage correction
methods.consequence: Completing 10 accepted requests still leaves 90 of 100 eligible requests unserved. Accepted-request completion is 100%; eligible-request coverage is 10%.

nodes.text: Accepted-request completion and eligible-request coverage answer different questions. Their different denominators account exactly for the apparently conflicting judgments.

children.text: Under the concern that eligible requests receive service, the acceptance-based score excludes the ninety unserved requests. Perfecting that score alone preserves their exclusion.
The coverage judgment changes without making the completion count false. It exposes the missing service; it does not itself supply that service.

nodes.text: A method can be exactly right about a question that no longer deserves to govern the undertaking. Purpose, beneficiaries, values, and the admitted alternatives can change what counts as an adequate result.

children.text: Publishing dissent's substance while withholding unnecessary identity satisfies the stipulated review and privacy obligations together. The conflict came from bundling two independently changeable fields.

A route that completes a task in two effort units and supplies valued understanding can be preferable to a one-unit route without that understanding. Task time alone does not rank the added consequence.
